title: fix(metadata-protocol): the search palette titles a hit by nameField before the deprecated titleFormat
body:
Fixes #24087

Clause-②: no

## What changed

`searchAll` (`GET /api/v1/search`, the console's global search palette) now titles a hit in this order: the primary-title pointer (`nameField`, then the deprecated alias `displayNameField`), then the `titleFormat` template, then the conventional name fields, then first/last name, then the record id. Before, `renderTitle` rendered `titleFormat` first and returned it whenever every placeholder resolved. ADR-0079 D3 says "an explicit `nameField` takes precedence over it", and the spec's `titleFormat` describe says the same.

- `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts`: in `renderTitle`, the pointer is read before the template. The comment above it now states the new order and why. The pointer moved out of the conventional candidate list; the list is otherwise unchanged.
- `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.search-title-namefield.test.ts`: the old pin `titleFormat still outranks the pointer` asserted the defect. It is replaced by a `[#24087]` block (below).
- `packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts`: `SearchAllHitSchema.title`'s describe stated the old order (`titleFormat` first). This change made it false, so it now states the new order. `content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx` is regenerated from it (`check:generated --fix`, the `check:docs` artifact only, two table rows).
- One changeset: `patch` for `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` and `@objectstack/spec`.

**File-surface note.** The claim fences out `packages/spec`, naming `resolveDisplayField` and the `titleFormat` describe; both are untouched. The `SearchAllHitSchema.title` describe is a third spec site: it is the published contract of the very reader this PR changes, and the reorder made its text false. The dev rules require fixing a shipped statement the change makes false, so it is fixed here (describe text only, no shape change) and named in the report.

## H1 measured: a provisioned `nameField` outranks `titleFormat`

`provisionPrimary` runs designate-only at the registry's materialization seam (`packages/objectql/src/registry.ts`, `materializeBaseLayer`). It stamps `nameField` on any object that has a title-eligible field. `ObjectTitleCompleteness.status`'s docblock in `spec/src/data/display-name.ts` records that authorship cannot be recovered after that stamp: "'the author wrote `nameField`' and 'the read derived `nameField`' are the same bytes". So `searchAll`, which reads `registry.getAllObjects()`, cannot tell an authored pointer from a stamped one. `resolveDisplayField` does not read `titleFormat` at all.

Mirroring it means `titleFormat` titles a row only when (a) the object has no title-eligible field, so nothing is stamped, or (b) the pointer's value is empty on that row. This is wider than "an explicit nameField". It was settled by the four axes and is listed in the report's `open_questions`. In short: the key is deprecated and lint-warned (`title-format-retired`), ADR-0079 sets the direction, and the reader cannot see authorship. The changeset gives the migration ADR-0079 prescribes for an author who wants a composite title: a text formula designated as `nameField`.

## Pins

All in `protocol.search-title-namefield.test.ts`. Each fixture goes through the real `provisionPrimary(..., { synthesize: false })`, so the pins see the body the registry serves:

1. **THE PIN.** The object declares both `titleFormat: '{process_name} · {record_id}'` and `nameField: 'display_title'` (a text formula). It is titled `Discount Sign-off · opp_45`, and `not.toBe('flow:deal_desk · opp_45')`.
2. **Control.** An object with only `titleFormat` and no title-eligible field gets no stamp, and the template still renders (`Order 42`).
3. **Control.** An empty pointer value falls through to the template, not to the id.
4. **Measured H1 consequence.** An object with only `titleFormat` plus a text field is titled by the stamped pointer (`TK-9`).
5. The existing `[#8786]` block is unchanged and still green. It includes an object with neither key, which falls back to `name` as before.

**Ablation (one run, source-resolved).** The test imports `./protocol.js` relatively, so it reads `src/` and no `dist/` leg applies. The mutation went through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`: the pointer guard was given `&& typeof titleFormatSource !== 'string'`, which restores template-first. The anchor went 1 → 0 and the marker 0 → 1, and the blob changed `375717c98f5d` → `cd9eb0ea1a25`. Result: **2 failed | 7 passed**, namely THE PIN and pin 4, as predicted. Restore: blob equals HEAD (`375717c98f5d`) and `git diff HEAD` is empty.

**Real engine.** The pin runs over the boundary double this file already uses, not a real ObjectQL. `metadata-protocol` cannot import `@objectstack/objectql` (objectql depends on it, a package cycle; see the header of `objectql/src/global-search-palette-recall.test.ts`). The real-engine home is in `packages/objectql`, outside this claim's file surface. Using the real `provisionPrimary` transform is the part of the engine that decides this behaviour.

## Census: other title readers that read `titleFormat` first

| Site | Reads `titleFormat` first? | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `metadata-protocol` `searchAll` `renderTitle` | **was yes, fixed here** | this PR |
| `spec` `resolveDisplayField` / `resolveRecordDisplayName` / `objectql` `resolveRecordTitle` | no, never reads it | `display-name.ts`: `nameField ?? displayNameField ?? derived` |
| `metadata-core` `object-schema-fls-references.ts` | not a title reader | collects the field references of the template for FLS |
| `lint` `validate-record-title.ts` and friends | not a title reader | warns `title-format-retired` |
| objectui renderers (calendar / kanban card title, record H1) | **yes, by the repo's own description; not measured** | `spec/src/ui/view.zod.ts` docblocks state the objectui chain as `titleFormat → displayNameField → type-aware derivation → 'Untitled'`; the liveness ledger records `titleFormat` as `live` via objectui interpolation. objectui is outside this session's scope, so this is a lead for the seat, not a reading. |

In this repository, `searchAll` was the only runtime reader that rendered `titleFormat`. The remaining family is the objectui display-name chain. It is reported in `out_of_scope_findings` as one family, and nothing in it is changed here.

## Acceptance notes

- Objects whose palette title changes with this PR are those that declare `titleFormat` beside a title-eligible field (stamped or authored `nameField`). `sys_approval_request` (the card's case, which declares `nameField: 'display_title'`) is measured by THE PIN's fixture shape. The roughly 30 other `*.object.ts` files declaring `titleFormat` were not measured one by one. Some `sys_*` prefixes are skipped by the palette entirely (`sys_audit_log`, `sys_activity`, `sys_presence`, …).
- `objectql/src/registry.ts` has a comment saying title-less system tables "keep resolving their title on read via `resolveDisplayField` / `titleFormat`". It stays accurate.
